definition.label: Snap a construction to a point
definition.description: Align the chosen point of the FIRST moving member with an exact destination point of the same family. Both local frames coincide, with turn in degrees about destination +Y. Move 1–15 distinct idle creations as one rigid arrangement, with optional relative scale (omitted means 1); include every connected member. The destination must be outside that list. Use current revisions for all members and destination. Pause physics and stop member/destination playback, grips and authoring. place only changes poses; join also adds an ordinary fixed connection from the first member to the destination, using explicit break limits (zero means unbreakable). The first member must then use solid/bouncy physics and have no outgoing connection; never silently replace an existing link. One save/Undo includes the live destination pose and the whole moving arrangement. Failed admission or pre-acceptance preparation changes nothing. Temporary edits stay in the fork; Stop does not undo completed edits. Snap points do not enforce occupancy, collision-free placement, nearest-point selection or chess rules. Subsequent point edits do not alter the accepted connection frames. Book controls, user programs and the agent call this same operation. Current member and destination poses are sampled when admitted to preparation; only those bodies are then held until native application or cancellation. A changed frame during preparation invalidates the request. Outside temporary play, prepares and publishes its save in the background with one Undo edit. Completion confirms native application and saving. Once preparation begins, newer authored changes invalidate its candidate. Cancellation before native acceptance leaves the requested edit unapplied. After acceptance, stopping cannot retract the edit or its pending save. A save conflict preserves files, blocks further saves and requires inspection; never blindly replay it. Runtime clock and viewer movement continue. Concurrent persisted object edits enter preparation in arrival order after earlier saves drain, without copying a waiting candidate. Stopping or invalidating a waiter releases its place; target changes while waiting require a new request. In a temporary room, changes the live room and local Undo; a kept snapshot makes it durable. Other objects keep running.

definition.label: Observe one saved object
definition.description: Read one exact saved object's display metadata without selecting, loading, moving or editing it. Uses the same projection as the room view, independently of which objects that view lists. objectRevision guards saved edits, not live frame changes. position is the current authored-frame origin when positionSource=live; otherwise it is the saved origin. runtimeState distinguishes active, inactive and unavailable native instances. held, simulating and animated describe an active grab, rigid simulation and recipe playback; false on a dormant object does not mean its saved recipe is stopped. color is the effective root tint, not sampled pixels or every part/material. Use component facts for full physics, placement, animation and appearance settings. Missing saved IDs return unavailable; use object.presence to explicitly distinguish missing from dormant. Reads do not acquire native resources or grant editing authority.
